docs/config.md:31:| WEBDIR | Set a custom location for your web or public files.  This is the root directory from which the web server will host your files and the root directory from which PHP-FPM will look for your PHP files.  Defaults to `htdocs`.  Other common settings are `public`, `static` or `html`.  Path is relative to `/home/vcap/app`. |

docs/usage.md:7:The easiest way to use the build pack is to put your assets and PHP files into a directory and push it to CloudFoundry.  When you do this, the build pack will take your files and automatically move them into the `WEBDIR` (defaults to `htdocs`) folder, which is the directory where your chosen web server looks for the files.

docs/usage.md:25:This comes with a catch.  If your project legitimately has a `lib` directory, these files will not be publicly available because the build pack does not copy a top-level `lib` directory into the `WEBDIR` folder.  If your project has a `lib` directory that needs to be publicly available then you have two options.

docs/usage.md:29:In your project folder, create an `htdocs` folder (or whatever you've set for `WEBDIR`).  Then move any files that should be publicly accessible into this directory.  In the example below, the `lib/controller.php` file is publicly accessible.

docs/usage.md:76:The second option is to pick a different name for the `LIBDIR`.  This is a configuration option that you can set (it defaults to `lib`).  Thus if you set it to something else, like `include` your application's `lib` directory would no longer be treated as a special directory and it would be placed into `WEBDIR` (i.e. become public).
docs/usage.md:80:Beyond the `WEBDIR` and `LIBDIR` directories, the build pack also supports a `.bp-config` directory and a `.extensions` directory.
